q: The home health nurse is caring for a 26-year-old client who has pulmonary tuberculosis and is receiving newly prescribed streptomycin 1 gram intramuscular (IM) once daily. Which of the following actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
o: Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.
Tell the client to contact the primary health care provider if the stool is black.
Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen for fever and headache.
Inform the client that there is no need for a follow-up visit once the medication is completed.
Advise the client to continue streptomycin therapy before any procedures that may require anesthesia.
r:
Correct:
• “Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.” – Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside and can damage the 8th cranial nerve (hearing and balance).
• “Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen…” – Acetaminophen is the safer choice for fever and headache; NSAIDs add kidney risk to an aminoglycoside.

Not correct:
• Black stool is not an expected effect of streptomycin.
• Follow-up visits are still needed after treatment (TB therapy is long and monitored).
• Streptomycin can increase the effect of anesthesia and muscle relaxants, so the client should tell the provider rather than simply continue it before procedures.

(From your class slides: Respiratory, slide 27.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The acetaminophen option is the least certain part of this key.

q: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff about post operative care for the client following abdominal surgery. Which content should the nurse speak about in the in-service? Select all that apply.
o: “Therapeutic touch is an effective way to decrease postoperative abdominal pain.”
“Total body relaxation is an effective adjunct for postoperative pain management.”
“The nursing process is linear throughout the postoperative care of clients who have had abdominal surgery.”

“The nurse’s priority is to check on the client who had abdominal surgery and returned to the unit just now and then check on the client who is requesting pain medication and returned from abdominal surgery 12 hours ago.”
r:
Correct:
• Therapeutic touch and total body relaxation are accepted non-drug adjuncts for post-operative pain.
• The newly returned post-operative client is seen first (airway, vital signs, bleeding) before the client at 12 hours who wants pain medication.

Not correct: The nursing process is not linear; it is continuous and cyclical, so assessment and evaluation keep repeating.

(From your class slides: GI, slide 32.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The therapeutic touch option is the least certain part of this key.

q: The nurse is preparing to teach an in-service for nursing staff and students about total parenteral nutrition. Which information should the nurse include in the in-service? Select all that apply.
o: “Clients with paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea are candidates for parenteral nutrition.”
“Total parenteral nutrition is delivered for the client through a gastrostomy or nasogastric tube.”
“Protein, electrolyte, and glucose nutritional imbalances may be supplemented with total parenteral nutrition.”
“Clients who need long-term nutritional supplementation will receive total parenteral nutrition via IV solutions comprised of 5% dextrose.”
r:
Correct: TPN is for clients who cannot use the GI tract (for example paralytic ileus or severe diarrhea) and can supplement protein, electrolytes and glucose.

Not correct:
• Tube feeding through a gastrostomy or nasogastric tube is enteral nutrition; TPN is given by IV.
• Long-term TPN is given through a central line in concentrated dextrose solutions; 5% dextrose supplies too few calories.

(From your class slides: GI, slide 33.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: The nurse has taught a client who has hypertension and a body mass index of 28. Which of the following statements by the client would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching?
o: “I should limit my sodium intake to 3300 mg per day.”
“I will participate in a maximum of 1 hour of exercise per week.”
“I can drink the maximum of 3 beverages that contain alcohol per day.”
“I am going to eat less calories per day by following the Mediterranean diet.”
r:
Correct: A lower-calorie heart-healthy eating pattern such as the Mediterranean diet supports weight loss, which lowers blood pressure.

Not correct:
• Sodium should be limited to about 2 g a day, not 3300 mg (class slide 5).
• Aerobic exercise should be increased; 1 hour a week is too little.
• Alcohol should be limited; 3 drinks a day is too many.

(From your class slides: Cardiac, slide 46.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has severe anemia and requires a transfusion of packed red blood cells (PRBCs). Which of the following four actions should the nurse plan to take?
o: Check vital signs before transfusion.
Insert an 18-gauge intravenous (IV) line.
Prime the blood tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride.
Transfuse the PRBCs within 6 hours.
Check the expiration date of the PRBCs with a second nurse.
r:
Correct: Take baseline vital signs, use a large-bore (18-gauge) IV, prime the tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride only, and verify the blood product and expiration with a second licensed nurse.

Not correct: A unit of PRBCs should be completed within 4 hours of leaving the blood bank; 6 hours is too long.

(From your class slides: Hematology, slide 14.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: A client has Diabetes Insipidus. Which nursing intervention is essential for monitoring this condition?
o: Inserting a Foley catheter
Measuring intake and output
Analyzing blood glucose levels
Sending a urine specimen to the lab
r:
Correct: Diabetes insipidus causes very large volumes of dilute urine (2–20 L a day), so measuring intake and output is essential, along with daily weights.

Not correct: A Foley is not routinely needed, and blood glucose is not the problem; diabetes insipidus is unrelated to diabetes mellitus.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH).  Which of the following assessment findings would indicate that the client is developing a complication?
o: A weight loss of 3 pounds in 4 days
Observance of neck vein distention
A decrease in blood pressure
An increase in urine output
r:
Correct: In SIADH the body retains water, so neck vein distention is a sign of fluid overload.

Not correct: Weight loss, lower blood pressure and increased urine output are not expected with water retention (SIADH gives low urine output, weight gain and low serum sodium).

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 9.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: The nurse is assessing a client who has possible Cushing’s syndrome.  The nurse expects to find:
o: hypotension.
thick, coarse skin.
truncal obesity.
weight gain in arms and legs.
r:
Correct: Cushing's syndrome causes truncal obesity (with thin arms and legs), a rounded face, hypertension, muscle wasting and carbohydrate intolerance.

Not correct: Hypotension is seen in Addison's disease; thick, coarse skin in hypothyroidism; and the extremities are thin, not heavy, in Cushing's.

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 17.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: A nurse is educating on blood sugar control to the client who has uncontrolled diabetes that their vision may be impaired from:
o: Prolonged periods of hyperglycemia
Frequent injections of regular insulin
Lens opacity
Corneal dryness
r:
Correct: Prolonged hyperglycemia damages the small vessels of the retina (diabetic retinopathy) and can change the lens, impairing vision. Good glucose control protects the eyes.

Not correct: Insulin injections do not cause vision problems; lens opacity (cataract) and corneal dryness are not the effect of high blood glucose being taught here.

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 22.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: Hemoglobin A1C provides information on glucose control over the past:
o: 20 to 40 days
50 to 65 days
60 to 85 days
90-120 days
r:
Correct: The hemoglobin A1C reflects average glucose control over about 90–120 days (roughly 3 months), the life span of red blood cells.

Not correct: The shorter time frames are too short.

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 23.)

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has pheochromocytoma.  Which of the following is the nurse most likely to assess?
o: Constricted pupils
Blood glucose level of 130 mg/dl
Bradycardia
Blood pressure of 176/88 mm Hg
r:
Correct: A pheochromocytoma releases excess catecholamines, causing hypertension (176/88 mm Hg), tachycardia, headache, sweating and anxiety.

Not correct: Constricted pupils and bradycardia are the opposite effects, and a glucose of 130 mg/dL is not a key finding.

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 25.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: The nurse is teaching a client who has diabetes mellitus (type 2) and a prescription for extended-release metformin. Select 2 statements the nurse should make.
o: “You may chew the tablet if you experience any difficulty swallowing.”
“You need to carry emergency identification and a glucagon kit at all times.”
“You should contact the physician if you notice the metformin tablet in the stool.”
“You will need to discontinue the medication for any procedure that requires a contrast agent.”
r:
Correct:
• “You will need to discontinue the medication for any procedure that requires a contrast agent.” – Metformin is held around contrast because of kidney injury and lactic acidosis risk.
• “You need to carry emergency identification and a glucagon kit…” – the likely intended second answer for this select-two item.

Not correct:
• Extended-release tablets must be swallowed whole, never chewed.
• The empty tablet shell can appear in the stool and is harmless; there is no need to call.

(From your class slides: Endocrine, slide 26.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The glucagon-kit option is the least certain part of this key (metformin alone rarely causes low blood sugar).

q: The nurse in the community clinic is caring for a 70-year-old client who has been wearing new bilateral hearing aids for 2 weeks. Which of the following should the nurse include in the client’s care plan?
o: Check the client’s dexterity with hearing aid use.
Communicate with the client above the client’s eye level.
Speak with the client using loud, high-pitched tones.
Remind the client to take off the glasses while wearing hearing aids.
r:
Correct: A new hearing-aid user needs the nurse to check that the client can handle and adjust the devices (dexterity) and has realistic expectations.

Not correct:
• Speak at eye level, face to face, not above it.
• Use a normal, lower-pitched tone; loud, high-pitched speech is harder to understand and can be distorted.
• Glasses can be worn with hearing aids, and the client does not need to remove them.

(From your class slides: Neurological, slide 80.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)

q: The nurse has taught a client who has sustained a right tibial fracture and had an external fixation device applied 36 hours ago. Which of the following statements by the client would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching? Select all that apply.
o: “I will use chlorhexidine to clean around the pins.”
“I should limit my daily consumption of foods high in vitamin D.”
“I should expect to see some redness around the external pins.”
“I know that the metal rods help steady my leg fracture as it is healing.”
“I will notify my doctor if I experience increased pressure to the point of pain around my heel.”
r:
Correct:
• Pin sites are cleaned with an antiseptic such as chlorhexidine, using aseptic technique.
• The metal frame holds the fracture steady while it heals.
• Increasing pressure and pain, for example around the heel, may signal compartment syndrome and must be reported.

Not correct:
• Vitamin D (and calcium) helps bone healing, so it should not be limited.
• Redness at the pin sites should be reported as a possible infection rather than accepted as normal.

(From your class slides: Musculoskeletal, slide 22.)
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The pin-site redness item is the least certain part of this key.
